description: Fixture behind the mock web_search tool. It simulates a search engine: mixed-quality pages with publish dates, including stale pages (2020 Mars plan, 2024 Bitcoin forecast) that a careful fact-checker must not treat as current.

pages.title: NASA and ESA outline Mars Sample Return campaign with launches in 2026
pages.snippet: NASA and ESA plan to launch the Mars Sample Return lander and Earth Return Orbiter in 2026, bringing Perseverance's samples back to Earth in the early 2030s.

pages.title: Independent review: Mars Sample Return could cost up to $11 billion
pages.snippet: An independent review board found the Mars Sample Return mission could cost $8 billion to $11 billion, with samples unlikely to return before 2040 under the existing plan; NASA paused parts of the program.

pages.title: NASA unveils two cheaper options for Mars Sample Return, return now 2035-2039
pages.snippet: NASA announced two possible architectures for Mars Sample Return, using a sky-crane lander or a commercial heavy-lift lander, with samples returning between 2035 and 2039. A final decision was delayed to 2026.

pages.title: Analysts: Bitcoin could hit $200,000 by the end of 2025
pages.snippet: Several analysts forecast that Bitcoin could reach $200,000 by the end of 2025, citing ETF inflows and the halving cycle.

pages.title: Bitcoin sets record above $126,000
pages.snippet: Bitcoin climbed to a record of about $126,000 on October 6, 2025 before pulling back; the price fell well short of the $200,000 forecasts made earlier in the year.

pages.title: Nvidia becomes first company worth $5 trillion
pages.snippet: Nvidia became the first company to reach a $5 trillion market capitalization on October 29, 2025, extending its lead in the AI chip boom.

pages.title: Perseverance rover lands safely in Jezero Crater
pages.snippet: NASA's Perseverance rover touched down in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021, beginning its mission to search for signs of ancient life and collect samples.

pages.title: How GitLab runs an all-remote company with a public handbook
pages.snippet: GitLab's public handbook runs to thousands of pages and documents nearly every process, a model other remote companies such as Automattic and Doist cite for async, documentation-first work.

pages.title: Amazon orders corporate staff back to the office five days a week
pages.snippet: Amazon told corporate employees to return to the office five days a week starting January 2, 2025, one of the largest return-to-office mandates among big employers.

pages.title: Remote-capable workers: hybrid remains the dominant model
pages.snippet: Surveys of remote-capable US employees find about half work hybrid, roughly a quarter fully remote, and the rest on-site, with little change over the past two years.

pages.title: FDA's AI-enabled medical device list passes 1,200 entries
pages.snippet: The FDA's updated list of AI-enabled medical devices now includes more than 1,200 authorized devices, most of them in radiology, all reviewed through 510(k), De Novo or PMA pathways.

pages.title: FDA permits first autonomous AI diagnostic device, IDx-DR
pages.snippet: The FDA permitted marketing of IDx-DR, the first device authorized to provide a screening decision for diabetic retinopathy without a clinician also interpreting the images.

pages.title: Telehealth use stabilizes at 38 times pre-pandemic levels
pages.snippet: Telehealth utilization has stabilized at levels 38 times higher than before the COVID-19 pandemic, as the pandemic accelerated adoption of digital health tools.

pages.title: Study finds racial bias in widely used health algorithm
pages.snippet: Researchers found a commercial algorithm used to guide care for millions of patients underestimated the needs of Black patients because it was trained on historical cost data.

pages.title: Hospitals deploy AI triage to flag urgent scans
pages.snippet: Hospitals are using AI to prioritize X-rays and CT scans with urgent findings such as strokes and collapsed lungs, moving them to the top of radiologists' worklists.

pages.title: Why most startups should bootstrap first
pages.snippet: Bootstrapped founders keep control and are forced to find revenue early; venture-backed founders trade equity and some control for speed, and face pressure from investors for an exit.

pages.title: When will humans land on Mars?
pages.snippet: NASA targets crewed Mars missions no earlier than the late 2030s; private timelines have repeatedly slipped and no date is firm.
